bugs.text: Every sprite definition is mk([ [rows...], {palette}) with the outer frames array never closed; the script fails to parse ('Unexpected token )' at line 80), so nothing runs: blank black page, no title, no game (confirmed by result.json and all screenshots).

Challenging stage: only updateChallenge runs, so the player cannot move, tryFire refuses (mode!=='play'), and there is no bullet-vs-enemy check; hits and waveHits are never incremented, so the stage is an unplayable fly-by with 0 hits and no bonus.
Losing one half of the dual fighter decrements lives, costing a reserve ship that the rescued fighter never added.
Capture is instant (player explodes, captive appears above boss); no pull-up into the beam.
Formation breathes all the time instead of only after it is complete.
Stage badges show a single flag with a number, not the arcade's combination of 1/5/10/20/30/50 badges.

summary: The design is compact and sensibly structured. It has a fixed-timestep loop, Bezier entry/dive/return paths, breathing formation, tractor beam with capture/rescue/dual fighter, escort scoring and synthesized sounds, so if it ran it would be a reasonably faithful though simplified Galaga. But it does not run. All four pixel-art sprite literals leave the outer frames array unclosed, which is a parse error at line 80. The harness shows the error at load and a black screen in every capture, so the delivered file is not playable at all. Adding the four missing brackets makes it parse. Even then, the challenging stages are broken because the player is frozen and hits are never counted. There are smaller rule slips too: the dual-half loss costs a life, the capture has no pull-up, and the badges are simplified.
